proposed_comments.title: Make theme-listener initialization transactional
proposed_comments.body:
### Make theme-listener initialization transactional

**Severity:** `high`

`ThemeListener` starts the first WMI watcher before the second watcher and the initial theme reads have completed, but the constructor has no rollback path if a later `Start()` or read fails. Mouse Without Borders creates this listener during tray-form startup, so an unavailable theme-notification service can leave an active watcher behind even though startup should continue with the current icon.

Create both watchers in locals, attach handlers and start them inside a guarded initialization block, and assign the fields only after both watchers and the initial reads succeed. On failure, detach and dispose both locals, then let the caller log the failure and continue initializing the form.

confidence.rationale: The upstream constructor starts watchers sequentially without rollback, while the changed Mouse Without Borders startup path constructs the listener directly during form initialization. The fork fixed this exact failure mode and the fix is absent from the upstream head.

proposed_comments.title: Limit propagation to supported modules and fix tray icon lifetimes
proposed_comments.body:
**Affected code:**
- `src/settings-ui/Settings.UI.Library/ThemeAdaptiveTrayIconFanOut.cs` - `ApplyToModules`, `ApplyAwake`, `ApplyZoomIt`, and `ApplyPowerDisplay`
- `src/settings-ui/Settings.UI/ViewModels/GeneralViewModel.cs` - the general-setting fan-out call
- `src/modules/MouseWithoutBorders/App/Form/frmScreen.cs` - `ChangeIcon`
- `src/settings-ui/Settings.UI/Strings/en-us/Resources.resw` - the general setting description

**Problem:** The new general toggle writes and broadcasts `show_theme_adaptive_tray_icon` to Awake, ZoomIt, PowerDisplay, and Mouse Without Borders, but this PR only adds a Mouse Without Borders consumer; the other modules either do not deserialize the property or do not rebuild their tray icon from it. The UI therefore promises cross-module behavior that does not exist. Separately, `ChangeIcon` keeps the default bitmap alive on the non-adaptive path because disposal is conditional on `disposeBitmap`, and the adaptive path performs theme work in a way that must preserve ownership of the handle-backed icon.

**Why it matters:** Users can enable a setting that silently has no effect in several modules, while repeated normal tray updates leak GDI resources. This can eventually exhaust desktop handles and makes the new setting unsafe to advertise as a global feature.

**Suggested change:**
1. Either add complete, tested consumers for every module named by the setting, or keep the general setting and localized text scoped to the modules implemented by this change and remove the unsupported fan-out/interop notifications.
2. In `ChangeIcon`, use a clear ownership rule: dispose every temporary bitmap after creating the tray icon, and release any owned icon handle at the matching lifetime boundary without disposing shared resources.
3. Keep the non-adaptive path free of unnecessary system-theme registry reads and add regression coverage for repeated default-icon updates, adaptive refreshes, and unsupported-module settings.

**Verification:** Build the exact upstream Settings and Mouse Without Borders projects, run focused tray/settings tests, and manually toggle the setting with the main tray icon both visible and hidden. Confirm only implemented consumers change and repeated icon updates do not increase GDI handle usage.
